influence_signal.instructions: Read the span text at state.span.text, using state.context.before and state.context.after only as surrounding context. Classify which single influence-taxonomy pattern, if any, is most clearly present in the span itself. Do not judge whether the underlying claim is true. Do not evaluate the speaker's character.

is_quoted_or_attributed.instructions: Read the span text at state.span.text. Return a high value if the span text reads as a direct quotation or a paraphrase attributed to a named or described speaker, rather than the surrounding author's own narration. Return a low value if the span reads as the author's own statement.
criteria: quoted or attributed to a speaker other than the narrating author

is_checkable_claim.instructions: Read the span text at state.span.text. Return a high value if the span asserts a specific, checkable fact (a number, a date, a named event, a direct quotation of what someone said) rather than an opinion, question, or general description.
criteria: contains a specific, checkable factual assertion

claim_kind.instructions: Only meaningful when is_checkable_claim is high. Read the span text at state.span.text and classify the kind of checkable claim it makes.
